To gain size while weight lifting there is an optimal way to do this. Most weight lifters feel compelled to do more of a strength training style instead of bodybuilding. Endurance is the other goal that generally involves spending more time using less weight.

For a good bodybuilding workout you must think "go slow to grow." When doing a repetition you should spend about 2 seconds going down, 2 seconds going up, and hold a second at the top of the motion. Studies suggested 6-8 repetitions are optimal for muscle growth. You will need to do 3 sets of repetitions separated by about 2 minutes. You can do each muscle once every 5-7 days. Remember, that you're not trying to lift the weight up and down or see how much weight you can put on there. You're trying to wear your muscle out by moving weight up and down. Using the slow method will keep your weight totals down, which is actually good for avoiding injuries to your joints and such. When you are pushing weight up, you're using your muscle. When you are holding weight up, you're using your muscle. When you lower it down slowly, you're using your muscle.

As you get accustomed to a weight level, you need to start adding more to get worn out. You should take notes about your experience with the weight used the previous time. Was it easy?
